# ui::KeyCombo

Header: `winui/core/Input.hpp`.

A key and its modifiers, without the action it runs. Menu items, app-bar buttons and commands carry their shortcut in it. The key combination fires app-wide ([Element::handle_global_shortcut()](../tree/element.md#handle_global_shortcut)) and its [text()](#text) is shown beside the item. Key::Unknown is no shortcut. Written the way the menu shows it, `ui::Ctrl + ui::Shift + ui::Key::N`, or as a bare key, `ui::Key::F4`. Alt key combinations work, except the ones the system owns (Alt+F4, Alt+Space, Alt+Tab, Alt+Esc), which never reach the window.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::KeyCombo save = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::S;

const std::string hint = save.text(); // "Ctrl+S", what a menu shows beside the label

// In a key handler: is this the key combination?
window.on_key_preview([save](const ui::KeyEvent& event)
{
    if (save.matches(event))
    {
        save_document();
        return ui::Handled;
    }
    return ui::NotHandled;
});
```

## key

```cpp
Key key = Key::Unknown
```

The key; Unknown means "no shortcut".

## modifiers

```cpp
ModifierKeys modifiers {}
```

Exactly the modifiers that must be held.

## KeyCombo

```cpp
constexpr KeyCombo() = default
```

No shortcut.

## KeyCombo

```cpp
constexpr KeyCombo(Key k)
```

The key alone, so a field takes `ui::Key::F4`.

## KeyCombo

```cpp
constexpr KeyCombo(Key k, ModifierKeys mods)
```

The key with `mods` held: `ui::KeyCombo{ui::Key::S, {.ctrl = true}}`.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True for Key::Unknown, i.e. no shortcut assigned.

## matches

```cpp
bool matches(const KeyEvent& e) const
```

True if `e` is a key-down of exactly this key combination: the same key and exactly the same modifiers. Always false for an [empty()](#empty) combination and for key-up events.

## text

```cpp
std::string text() const
```

"Ctrl+S" ([shortcut_text()](namespace-ui.md#shortcut_text)); empty for an [empty()](#empty) combination.
